rationale: Compound: ⲙⲟⲩ ('water') + ⲛ̄- (genitive) + ϩⲱⲟⲩ (= ⲍⲱⲟⲩ 'rain'). 'Rain-water = downpour.' Used in cloud-rain simile of line 21-22.
Greek ἀρχιζωγράφος. Cosmological title applied to the sea acting as master-painter that depicts/paints the dragon-Error in its altered cosmic likeness. Pairs with ἀρχιτέκτων in same line.
Greek ἀρχιτέκτων. Master-builder title for the sea's architectonic role in fashioning the cosmos around the captured dragon.
Plural noun for minting-stamps or coin-impressions; collocated with ⲡⲧⲁⲃⲉϥ ('mold/seal') and ϩⲟⲗⲟⲕⲟⲧⲓⲛⲟⲥ ('gold solidus'). Likely Greek-derived numismatic term. Confidence moderate.
Greek ὁλοκότινος, the late-Roman/Byzantine gold solidus coin. Used in the smith-typology: a craftsman fashions multiple coin-stamps into a single icon.
Greek πέρας 'limit, end, boundary.' Cosmological-temporal term: the bounded outer-extent of the sea within which the seals of time are sealed.
Greek τροχός + ⲥⲓⲟⲩ 'star.' Standard Manichaean cosmological term for the rotating astral wheel from which the dragon is expelled. Cf. ⲡⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ ⲉⲧϣⲟⲟⲡ 'Wheel that exists' in glossary.
Verbal noun ⲡⲓ-ⲱⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'the throwing-forth.' Cosmogonic verb of expulsion. Distinct from ⲡⲱⲣⲭ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('separate forth') and ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('release').
From Coptic ⲉⲓⲱ 'wash.' With ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth' = thoroughly cleanse. Used here of the Father of Life cleansing the wheel of stars.

Cosmological enumeration of three loci of deceit (ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲗⲟⲡⲉ in earlier vocab). Recalls the 'three living words sent against three places of deceit' (sixth work of the Living Spirit) attested in earlier kephalaia.
Greek ἐνέργεια 'operation, working.' Lyc. ⲣⲣ for ⲣⲅ. Standard Manichaean technical term for the dynamic operation of the cosmic powers.
